hunks.baseline: Word had spread that the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi—or rather, the Blazing Fire Divine Dragon, Jin Taekyung—and the Huashan Divine Dragon, Cheongpung, were leaving, and people had gathered in clouds.
hunks.sol: Word had spread that the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi—or rather, the Blazing Fire Divine Dragon, Jin Taekyung—and the Huashan Divine Dragon, Cheongpung, were leaving, drawing people in like clouds.

hunks.baseline: Not only martial artists, but fearless commoners as well, had come out to see them off. The crowd stretched farther and farther, an endless tail that could not be counted.
hunks.sol: Not only martial artists but fearless commoners had come to see them off. The crowd stretched on and on, an endless procession too vast to count.

hunks.baseline: The murmuring noise gradually faded as the procession moved farther away.
hunks.sol: The clamor gradually faded as the procession moved farther away.

hunks.baseline: And on a deserted hilltop, a boy sitting on a tree stump and watching the entire scene suddenly spoke.
hunks.sol: On a deserted hilltop, a boy sat on a tree stump watching it all. He suddenly spoke.

hunks.baseline: “We certainly have. It’s tiring.”
hunks.sol: “We certainly have. It’s exhausting.”

hunks.sol: The boy, Mungyeong, watched his old disciple collapse onto the grass, breathing heavily, and muttered,

hunks.baseline: He was not talking about distance. Mungyeong was talking about the years they had traveled through.
hunks.sol: He wasn’t talking about distance. Mungyeong was talking about the years they had lived through.

hunks.sol: The old disciple wiped the sweat from his brow as though the scorching sun of that day were beating down on him once more.

hunks.baseline: The young and ambitious emperor changed the era name and attempted reforms, but the people, exhausted by the long civil war, were far too weary to heed the emperor’s will and take part in those reforms.
hunks.sol: The young, ambitious emperor changed the era name and sought to enact reforms, but the people were too exhausted by the long civil war to heed his will and take part.

hunks.baseline: “There was a drought, and swarms of locusts swept across the plains. The corpses of government soldiers and rebels filled the roads, and epidemics spread everywhere.”
hunks.sol: “Drought struck, and swarms of locusts swept across the plains. The corpses of government soldiers and rebels lay everywhere, and epidemics raged.”

hunks.baseline: Death gave birth to more death, and soon it devoured the entire continent.
hunks.sol: Death bred more death, until it engulfed the entire continent.

hunks.baseline: A young carpenter with the surname Dong could not escape the dark shadow that hung over the land, either.
hunks.sol: A young carpenter surnamed Dong could not escape the dark shadow cast over the land.

hunks.baseline: “I still think about that time from time to time.”
hunks.sol: “I still think about those days from time to time.”

hunks.baseline: The decades had changed more than just the landscape. The young carpenter who had lost his beloved wife and two children to the epidemic had since become an old physician.
hunks.sol: The passing decades had changed more than the landscape. The young carpenter who had lost his beloved wife and two children to the epidemic had since become an old physician.

hunks.baseline: “I wonder if I could have saved my family if I had been just a little faster. If I had found you sooner.”
hunks.sol: “I wonder whether I could have saved my family if I’d been just a little faster. If I’d found you sooner.”

hunks.baseline: Sitting on a hill close to the heavens and gazing at the drifting scraps of cloud, the old physician’s eyes had returned to those of the young carpenter.
hunks.sol: Sitting on a hill close to the heavens and gazing at the drifting wisps of cloud, the old physician’s eyes became those of the young carpenter once more.

hunks.baseline: “For as long as I have breath in my body.”
hunks.sol: “I will for as long as there is breath in my body.”

hunks.baseline: It had been only a single day.
hunks.sol: He had been only one day too late.

hunks.baseline: By the time the carpenter, dragging along his plague-stricken body, brought back the nameless old physician who had been staying in the slash-and-burn settlers’ village, everything was already too late.
hunks.sol: By the time the carpenter dragged his plague-stricken body to the village of slash-and-burn farmers and returned with the nameless old physician staying there, it was already over.

hunks.baseline: He cried for an entire day, then dug a pit to bury his family. And he made one request of the physician he had brought.
hunks.sol: He wept for an entire day, then dug a pit in which to bury his family. Afterward, he made one request of the physician he had brought.

hunks.baseline: Mungyeong answered in his blunt voice.
hunks.sol: Mungyeong answered bluntly.

hunks.baseline: It had hurt. Not because of pain that threatened his life, but because he could no longer see his beloved wife and children.
hunks.sol: It had hurt—not because his life hung in the balance, but because he would never see his beloved wife and children again.

hunks.baseline: “You were the one who made me stand again, Master.”
hunks.sol: “You were the one who helped me to my feet, Master.”

hunks.baseline: “I merely held out my hand. You were the one who took it and stood.”
hunks.sol: “I merely held out my hand. You were the one who chose to take it and stand.”

hunks.baseline: “I had to live. I had something to do.”
hunks.sol: “I had to live. I had found something I needed to do.”

hunks.baseline: The carpenter’s body should have died from the epidemic.
hunks.sol: The carpenter should have died from the epidemic as well.

hunks.baseline: But the physician cured him with medical knowledge unlike anything he had ever seen, and for the first time, the carpenter realized that even a human being could alter the birth, aging, sickness, and death ordained by heaven.
hunks.sol: But the physician cured him with medical arts unlike anything he had ever seen. For the first time, the carpenter realized that even a mere human could alter the birth, aging, sickness, and death ordained by heaven.

hunks.baseline: “I remember it differently. I remember you beckoning me to follow you, Master.”
hunks.sol: “I remember it differently. I remember you beckoning for me to follow you, Master.”

hunks.baseline: Thus, the young carpenter who had lost his family found a new goal, while the old physician who traveled the world caring for the sick and poor gained a new disciple.
hunks.sol: Thus, the young carpenter who had lost his family found a new purpose, while the old physician who wandered the realm caring for the powerless and poor gained a new disciple.

hunks.baseline: It was only much later that the carpenter, who had now become a physician himself, learned his master’s true identity.
hunks.sol: It was only much later that the carpenter, by then a physician himself, learned his master’s true identity.

hunks.baseline: “Slaughter Saint… It is a truly terrifying sobriquet. That was the first time you felt like a stranger to me, Master.”
hunks.sol: “Slaughter Saint… It is a truly terrifying sobriquet. That was the first time you ever felt like a stranger to me, Master.”

hunks.baseline: Mungyeong gazed into the distance with an emotionless expression.
hunks.sol: Mungyeong gazed into the distance, his expression unreadable.

hunks.baseline: “I have taken countless lives over the years. I was nothing more than an ugly slaughter demon hiding my past. I would have understood if you had left.”
hunks.sol: “I have taken more lives than I can count. I was nothing more than a vile killer who hid his past. I would have understood if you had left.”

hunks.baseline: “Perhaps I really would have. But I knew all too well what kind of person you were, Master.”
hunks.sol: “Perhaps I really might have. But I knew all too well what kind of person you were, Master.”

hunks.baseline: A moment later, his low voice continued.
hunks.sol: A moment later, the old disciple continued quietly.

hunks.baseline: “The Divine Physician. My master is known as the Divine Physician. You are not someone who would kill without reason.”
hunks.sol: “The Divine Physician. My master is the man known as the Divine Physician. You would never take a life without reason.”

hunks.baseline: It was a truth he had never told anyone, and one that no one had ever been willing to acknowledge.
hunks.sol: It was a truth he had never told anyone—and one no one had ever been willing to acknowledge.

hunks.baseline: He had lived as an assassin, taking countless lives with his own hands, whether they belonged to the orthodox faction, the unorthodox faction, or the Demonic Cult. And every one of those people had had a reason they deserved to die.
hunks.sol: He had lived as an assassin and taken countless lives with his own hands, whether they belonged to the orthodox faction, the unorthodox faction, or the Demonic Cult. Every one of them had deserved to die.

hunks.baseline: A Great Hero of the orthodox faction, renowned for his fairness and integrity, had made a hobby of raping and murdering women. A master of an unorthodox faction had slaughtered an entire village for fun.
hunks.sol: A Great Hero of the orthodox faction, renowned for his fairness and integrity, had made a hobby of raping and murdering women. A master of the unorthodox faction had slaughtered an entire village for amusement.

hunks.baseline: If the army of the Demonic Cult invading the Central Plains had not killed and destroyed indiscriminately, and if the greatest assassin under heaven had not stepped forward to kill those infamous demon heads because he could no longer stand by and watch, he could never have been called the Slaughter Saint.
hunks.sol: If the Demonic Cult’s army had not invaded the Central Plains, killing and destroying everything in its path, and if the greatest assassin under heaven had not finally stepped forward to kill its infamous demons, he would never have come to be called the Slaughter Saint.

hunks.baseline: “If I had not fought the Demonic Cult, the entire world would have pointed fingers at me. Just as it had always done.”
hunks.sol: “If I had not fought the Demonic Cult, the whole world would have pointed fingers at me. Just as it always had.”

hunks.baseline: The title of Slaughter Saint was merely an absolution granted by the orthodox faction that ruled the Murim—and praise for a powerful man.
hunks.sol: The sobriquet Slaughter Saint was merely absolution granted by the orthodox faction that now ruled Murim—and praise for a man of great strength.

hunks.baseline: Mungyeong had always been Mungyeong, but people neither knew nor wanted to know the truth hidden beneath the surface.
hunks.sol: Mungyeong had always been Mungyeong, yet people neither knew nor cared to know the truth hidden beneath the surface.

hunks.baseline: “It is all in the past. I wanted to leave the Murim, and I became a physician as I had intended. I will continue to do so.”
hunks.sol: “It is all in the past. I wished to leave Murim, so I became a physician as I had intended. And I will remain one.”

hunks.baseline: “Let’s go down. There are patients waiting for us.”
hunks.sol: “Let’s head down. There are patients waiting for us.”

hunks.baseline: He had just started walking, his voice dry, when—
hunks.sol: He had just taken his first step when the old disciple spoke.

hunks.baseline: Mungyeong came to an abrupt stop. Behind him, the old disciple’s voice continued.
hunks.sol: Mungyeong stopped dead. Behind him, the old disciple continued.

hunks.baseline: “The same thing that happened back then will happen again. Countless people will die or be injured. There will be countless people who have lost their parents or children, and the screams and deaths will never end.”
hunks.sol: “What happened back then will happen again. Countless people will die or be injured. People who have lost their parents or children will be everywhere, and the screams and deaths will never cease.”

hunks.baseline: “…I suppose I’ll be very busy. I should make preparations.”
hunks.sol: “…I suppose we’ll be very busy. We should make preparations.”

hunks.baseline: “I am a physician. Though I broke the promise I made to myself and killed when I had no other choice, I will never make that mistake again.”
hunks.sol: “I am a physician. Though I broke the promise I made to myself and took lives when I had no other choice, I will never make that mistake again.”

hunks.baseline: “Fighting is their responsibility, and treating the sick is ours. My heart left the Murim long ago.”
hunks.sol: “Fighting is their duty, and treating the sick is ours. In my heart, I left Murim long ago.”

hunks.baseline: “Then why did you never abandon your martial arts?”
hunks.sol: “Then why have you never abandoned your martial arts?”

hunks.baseline: It was a question he himself had carried for a long time. If he had wanted to leave the Murim because he hated killing, then it should have been right for him to abandon martial arts as well—the means by which he killed.
hunks.sol: It was a question he had carried for a long time. If he had wanted to leave Murim because he hated killing, he should also have cast aside martial arts—the means by which he killed.

hunks.baseline: Yet his martial arts had advanced even further. It was proof that he had been unable to let go of his attachment to them.
hunks.sol: Yet his martial arts had advanced even further. It was proof that he had been unable to sever his attachment to them.

hunks.baseline: *Why was that?*
hunks.sol: *Why?*

hunks.baseline: “You can treat hundreds, even thousands, of patients, Master. At the same time, you are capable of saving tens of thousands of lives.”
hunks.sol: “You can treat hundreds, even thousands, of patients, Master. But you are also someone capable of saving tens of thousands of lives at once.”

hunks.baseline: “Please prevent the coming war—not as the Slaughter Saint, but as the Divine Physician. This disciple will care for the patients here.”
hunks.sol: “Please prevent the coming war—not as the Slaughter Saint, but as the Divine Physician. This disciple will remain here and care for the patients.”

hunks.baseline: Mungyeong suddenly lifted his head and looked at the sky.
hunks.sol: Mungyeong lifted his head and looked at the sky.

hunks.baseline: With his blunt voice, he resumed his halted steps.
hunks.sol: With those blunt words, he resumed walking.

hunks.baseline: “I should go check on the patients. Come down slowly.”
hunks.sol: “I should go check on the patients. Take your time coming down.”

hunks.sol: As he descended the hill, Dongbong’s voice drifted after him.

hunks.sol: “Pointless. Murim is not where I belong.”

hunks.sol: Yet as the old disciple watched his master’s back recede into the distance, a faint smile formed on his lips.

hunks.baseline: “Please… stay well.”
hunks.sol: “Please… be well.”

hunks.sol: “What are you looking at?”
